substances.name: Taurine
substances.uses: Energy drinks, infant formula, cat-food nutrition.
substances.notes: The amino-sulfonic acid of bile and energy-drink fame.

substances.name: Creatine
substances.uses: Sports supplementation, muscle research.
substances.notes: The muscle-energy phosphate carrier supplement.

substances.name: Beta-alanine
substances.uses: Sports supplements (muscle carnosine), pre-workout tingles.
substances.notes: Non-proteinogenic beta amino acid; causes harmless face tingles.

substances.name: Monopotassium phosphate
substances.uses: Fertilisers, hydroponics, pH buffers, sports drinks.
substances.notes: Phosphorus-and-potassium plant feed.

substances.name: Hypophosphorous acid
substances.uses: Electroless nickel plating, pharmaceuticals, reductions.
substances.notes: Strong monobasic acid with two P-H bonds.

substances.name: Chlorous acid
substances.uses: Chlorite generation for bleaching paper.
substances.notes: Unstable mid oxyacid of chlorine.

substances.name: Hydrobromic acid
substances.uses: Making bromides, inorganic synthesis, alkylation catalysis.
substances.notes: Stronger acid than HCl by bond strength.

substances.name: Hydroiodic acid
substances.uses: Iodide chemistry, methylation catalysis, reductions.
substances.notes: One of the strongest simple acids; fumes readily.

substances.name: Beryllium hydroxide
substances.uses: Beryllium metal and oxide production.
substances.notes: Amphoteric hydroxide of the lightest alkaline earth.

substances.name: Lithium carbonate
substances.uses: Bipolar-disorder medicine, battery cathodes, glass and ceramics.
substances.notes: The original mood stabiliser and modern battery feedstock.

substances.name: Calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite)
substances.uses: Bone and tooth mineral, implants, toothpaste remineralisation.
substances.notes: Your skeleton is essentially this compound.

substances.name: Silver chloride
substances.uses: Photochemistry history, reference electrodes, antibacterial glass.
substances.notes: Darkens in light — the basis of early photography.

substances.name: Lead chromate
substances.uses: Historic yellow paint (Van Gogh era), now restricted.
substances.notes: The brilliant but toxic yellow of old masters.

substances.name: Prussian blue
substances.uses: Classic blue pigment, radiation (caesium) antidote, blueprinting.
substances.notes: The first modern synthetic pigment (1704).

substances.name: Copper(I) chloride
substances.uses: Organic catalysis (Sandmeyer), desulfurisation, flame colouring.
substances.notes: White salt that turns blue-green in air.

substances.name: Ferric ammonium citrate
substances.uses: Blueprint paper, food fortification, blueprints and photography.
substances.notes: Light-sensitive iron salt of classic blueprint paper.

substances.name: Calcium acetate
substances.uses: Concrete additives, keto therapy drug (as bivalent), vinegar chemistry.
substances.notes: Forms flammable acetone when dry-distilled — old trick.

substances.name: Magnesium carbonate
substances.uses: Climbing and gymnastics chalk, antacids, fireproofing, toothpaste.
substances.notes: Dries sweaty palms on the climbing wall.

substances.name: Aluminium phosphate
substances.uses: Vaccine adjuvant, ceramics, cement chemistry.
substances.notes: Immune-boosting adjuvant in many vaccines.

substances.name: Sodium iodide
substances.uses: Scintillation detectors, iodine supplements, organic synthesis.
substances.notes: Gamma-ray detectors use its crystals.

substances.name: Ammonium iron(III) sulfate
substances.uses: Mordant dyeing, etching, water treatment.
substances.notes: Purple alum crystal used in etching copper.

substances.name: Tetrasodium EDTA
substances.uses: Water softening, food preservative, chelation therapy, blood tubes.
substances.notes: Metal-grabbing molecule that locks up calcium and heavy metals.

substances.name: Potassium sodium tartrate
substances.uses: Piezoelectric history, Fehling's solution, baking powder history.
substances.notes: First piezoelectric crystal discovered.

substances.name: Sodium potassium tartrate tetrahydrate (Fehling component)
substances.uses: Sugar tests (Fehling's solution B).
substances.notes: Keeps copper dissolved in the classic aldehyde test.

substances.name: Copper(I) iodide
substances.uses: Organic synthesis, cloud seeding research, timber preservation.
substances.notes: White salt used in C-C coupling catalysis.

substances.name: Cobalt(II) chloride
substances.uses: Humidity indicator gels (blue to pink), invisible ink, catalysts.
substances.notes: The colour-changing moisture indicator of desiccator lids.

substances.name: Nickel(II) sulfate
substances.uses: Nickel electroplating, catalysts, ceramics colours.
substances.notes: The electrolyte of nickel plating baths.

substances.name: Tin(II) chloride
substances.uses: Tinning steel, mirror silvering, analytical reductions.
substances.notes: The mirror-maker's reducing agent.

substances.name: Potassium cyanide
substances.uses: Gold mining (restricted), casein historic uses, forensic case studies.
substances.notes: Extremely toxic salt; releases HCN with acids.

substances.name: Gold(III) chloride
substances.uses: Gold nanoparticle synthesis, gilding chemistry, histology.
substances.notes: The doorway to colloidal gold chemistry.

substances.name: Silver oxide
substances.uses: Button-cell batteries, Tollens' reagent prep, glass polishing.
substances.notes: Powers tiny watch batteries.

substances.name: Mercury(II) chloride
substances.uses: Historic antiseptic and preservative; laboratory reagent (restricted).
substances.notes: Infamous historic poison; now tightly controlled.

substances.name: Nitrogen triiodide
substances.uses: Chemistry-demonstration popularity (touch-sensitive cracking).
substances.notes: Dries into a solid that detonates on a feather's touch.

substances.name: Dinitrogen tetroxide
substances.uses: Hypergolic rocket propellant oxidiser (Proton, Apollo).
substances.notes: Ignites on contact with hydrazine fuels — rocket chemistry.

substances.name: Carbon suboxide
substances.uses: Research chemistry, organic synthesis oddity.
substances.notes: Cumulene oxide with linear O=C=C=C=O chain.

substances.name: Ammonium carbonate
substances.uses: Old-fashioned crisp cookies (smelling salts history).
substances.notes: Leavening that vanishes completely in baked goods.

substances.name: Urea peroxide
substances.uses: Teeth whitening, earwax softening drops, disinfection.
substances.notes: Stable solid peroxide for whitening gels.

substances.name: Calcium cyanamide
substances.uses: Slow-release nitrogen fertiliser, weed killer, steel nitriding.
substances.notes: Fertiliser that also inhibits weeds in the soil.

substances.name: Basic bismuth nitrate
substances.uses: Antidiarrhoeal medicines, cosmetic pearlescence, firework effects.
substances.notes: Stomach-soothing bismuth salt.

substances.name: Bismuth subsalicylate
substances.uses: Upset-stomach medicines (pink bismuth).
substances.notes: The pink liquid of travellers' stomach troubles.

substances.name: Aluminium chlorohydrate
substances.uses: Antiperspirants, water treatment, deodorants.
substances.notes: Blocks sweat ducts in antiperspirant sticks.

substances.name: Silver cyanide
substances.uses: Silver electroplating (restricted handling).
substances.notes: Plating-bath salt handled under strict cyanide rules.

substances.name: Potassium gold cyanide
substances.uses: Gold electroplating baths (jewellery, electronics).
substances.notes: The gold source of most plated contacts and jewellery.

substances.name: Nickel tetracarbonyl
substances.uses: Nickel refining (Mond process), research.
substances.notes: Deadly volatile liquid used to purify nickel metal.

substances.name: Iron pentacarbonyl
substances.uses: Anti-knock additive history, iron nanoparticle synthesis.
substances.notes: Orange liquid carbonyl of iron-nano chemistry.

substances.name: Tetrakis(triphenylphosphine)palladium
substances.uses: Suzuki and Heck cross-couplings in drug discovery.
substances.notes: The cross-coupling workhorse of modern medicinal chemistry.

substances.name: Methylmercury
substances.uses: Environmental toxicology case studies (Minamata).
substances.notes: Bioaccumulating neurotoxin of mercury-pollution history.

substances.name: Tetraethyllead
substances.uses: Leaded-petrol history (now banned nearly everywhere), aviation piston fuel.
substances.notes: The octane booster that poisoned a century.

substances.name: Diethylzinc
substances.uses: Semiconductor doping (MOCVD), atomic-layer deposition.
substances.notes: Spontaneously flammable zinc alkyl of chip making.

substances.name: Cytosine
substances.uses: Pyrimidine base in DNA and RNA; pairs with guanine.
substances.notes: One of the four letters of the genetic code; cytosine methylation switches genes on and off.

substances.name: Guanine
substances.uses: Purine base in DNA, RNA and GTP; pairs with cytosine.
substances.notes: Pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds, the strongest of the DNA base pairs.

substances.name: Thymine
substances.uses: Pyrimidine base found in DNA; pairs with adenine.
substances.notes: RNA replaces thymine with uracil, which is the same ring without the methyl group.

substances.name: Uracil
substances.uses: Pyrimidine base in RNA; pairs with adenine.
substances.notes: The RNA letter that takes the place of thymine in DNA.

substances.name: 2-Deoxyribose
substances.uses: Sugar component of DNA nucleotides.
substances.notes: Missing the 2-prime hydroxyl of ribose, which makes DNA more chemically stable than RNA.

substances.name: Adenosine
substances.uses: Building block of RNA and ATP; used as an antiarrhythmic drug.
substances.notes: Adenine joined to ribose; the core of ATP, ADP, AMP and cAMP.

substances.name: Guanosine
substances.uses: Building block of RNA; precursor to GMP and cGMP.
substances.notes: Guanine joined to ribose; its triphosphate GTP powers protein synthesis.

substances.name: Cytidine
substances.uses: Building block of RNA; precursor to cytidine nucleotides.
substances.notes: Cytosine joined to ribose; related drugs include cytarabine.

substances.name: Uridine
substances.uses: Building block of RNA; used in supplements and antiviral drugs.
substances.notes: Uracil joined to ribose; activated forms carry sugars into metabolism.

substances.name: Thymidine
substances.uses: DNA nucleoside; basis of antiviral drugs such as AZT.
substances.notes: Thymine joined to deoxyribose; the DNA counterpart of uridine.

substances.name: Adenosine triphosphate
substances.uses: Universal energy currency of cells; powers muscle contraction, transport and synthesis.
substances.notes: Hydrolysing one phosphate off ATP to make ADP releases the energy that drives most cell work.

substances.name: Adenosine diphosphate
substances.uses: ATP hydrolysis product; recycled back to ATP in respiration and photosynthesis.
substances.notes: Two phosphates; accepting one more phosphate rebuilds it into ATP.

substances.name: Adenosine monophosphate
substances.uses: RNA nucleotide and flavour enhancer; cyclised into the messenger cAMP.
substances.notes: One phosphate; a building block of RNA and of cyclic AMP.

substances.name: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide
substances.uses: Electron carrier in cellular respiration; central to redox metabolism.
substances.notes: Cycles between NAD+ and reduced NADH during glycolysis and the Krebs cycle.

substances.name: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate
substances.uses: Supplies reducing power (NADPH) for biosynthesis and antioxidant defence.
substances.notes: Carries an extra phosphate compared with NAD; NADPH drives fatty-acid and nucleotide synthesis.

substances.name: Flavin adenine dinucleotide
substances.uses: Electron carrier in the Krebs cycle and fatty-acid oxidation.
substances.notes: Built from riboflavin (vitamin B2); accepting two electrons gives FADH2.

substances.name: Coenzyme A
substances.uses: Carries acyl groups; central to fatty-acid metabolism and the Krebs cycle.
substances.notes: Its reactive thiol end forms acetyl-CoA, the gateway molecule of respiration.

substances.name: Glutathione
substances.uses: Master antioxidant; detoxifies peroxides and drugs and supports immune function.
substances.notes: A tripeptide of glutamate, cysteine and glycine; the main redox buffer inside cells.

substances.name: Ergocalciferol
substances.uses: Vitamin D supplement; regulates calcium absorption and bone health.
substances.notes: Made from ergosterol in fungi and yeast exposed to ultraviolet light.

substances.name: Menaquinone
substances.uses: Blood clotting and calcium regulation; produced by gut bacteria and fermented foods.
substances.notes: A family: MK-4 (C31H40O2) comes from animal foods and MK-7 (C46H64O2) from natto and cheese.

substances.name: Pyridoxal phosphate
substances.uses: Active form of vitamin B6; cofactor for amino-acid and neurotransmitter synthesis.
substances.notes: A Schiff-base-forming coenzyme at the heart of transamination reactions.

substances.name: Retinoic acid
substances.uses: Acne and leukaemia drug; controls gene expression during development.
substances.notes: The active metabolite of vitamin A; used as tretinoin in skincare.

substances.name: Creatinine
substances.uses: Waste product of muscle creatine; measured in blood and urine to assess kidney function.
substances.notes: A high blood creatinine level signals reduced kidney filtration.

substances.name: Uric acid
substances.uses: End product of purine breakdown; high levels cause gout and kidney stones.
substances.notes: Humans lack the enzyme uricase, so uric acid builds up; birds excrete it as a white paste.

substances.name: Hemoglobin
substances.uses: Oxygen transport in red blood cells; also carries some carbon dioxide back to the lungs.
substances.notes: Four globin subunits each hold a heme iron atom that binds oxygen reversibly; average molar mass about 64500.

substances.name: Chlorophyll a
substances.uses: Primary photosynthetic pigment of plants, algae and cyanobacteria.
substances.notes: A magnesium-centred porphyrin that absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.

substances.name: Chlorophyll b
substances.uses: Accessory photosynthetic pigment that widens the range of light captured.
substances.notes: Differs from chlorophyll a by an aldehyde group; gives leaves their olive-green tone.

substances.name: Heme
substances.uses: Oxygen-binding and electron-transfer cofactor in hemoglobin and cytochromes.
substances.notes: An iron-porphyrin ring; the central iron atom is what actually grabs the oxygen.

substances.name: DNA
substances.uses: Stores the genetic instructions of all living cells and many viruses.
substances.notes: A double helix of two antiparallel strands joined by A-T and G-C base pairs; average base pair about 660 g/mol.

substances.name: RNA
substances.uses: Carries genetic messages, builds proteins and can catalyse reactions as a ribozyme.
substances.notes: Usually single-stranded and uses uracil instead of thymine; about 340 g/mol per nucleotide.

substances.name: Galactose
substances.uses: Component of lactose and glycolipids; an energy source in dairy foods.
substances.notes: An aldohexose that is a mirror-image epimer of glucose; the other half of lactose.

substances.name: Glycogen
substances.uses: Stores glucose in the liver and muscles for quick energy release.
substances.notes: A highly branched glucose polymer; the body's short-term energy reserve.

substances.name: Lactulose
substances.uses: Laxative and liver-disease medicine; made by isomerising lactose.
substances.notes: A synthetic disaccharide of galactose and fructose that gut bacteria ferment.

substances.name: Acetonitrile
substances.uses: Solvent for HPLC and organic synthesis; intermediate in pharmaceutical manufacture.
substances.notes: A polar aprotic solvent that is flammable and toxic by ingestion or inhalation.

substances.name: Dimethyl sulfoxide
substances.uses: Polar aprotic solvent, cryoprotectant and topical anti-inflammatory.
substances.notes: Readily penetrates skin and freezes at about 18.5 degrees Celsius.

substances.name: Tetrahydrofuran
substances.uses: Ether solvent for polymers, Grignard reactions and 3D-printing resins.
substances.notes: Forms explosive peroxides on standing, so it is stored over an inhibitor.

substances.name: Styrene
substances.uses: Monomer for polystyrene, ABS plastic and synthetic rubber.
substances.notes: A reactive vinyl aromatic that is an irritant and a possible carcinogen.

substances.name: Bisphenol A
substances.uses: Monomer for polycarbonate plastics and epoxy resins.
substances.notes: An endocrine disruptor that is restricted in food-contact plastics in many countries.

substances.name: Polyvinyl alcohol
substances.uses: Water-soluble films, adhesives, textile sizing and 3D-printing support material.
substances.notes: Made by hydrolysing polyvinyl acetate; unusual among polymers for dissolving in water.

substances.name: Polyvinyl acetate
substances.uses: Wood glue, paints, adhesives and paper coatings.
substances.notes: The classic white school glue, made by polymerising vinyl acetate.

substances.name: Polyacrylonitrile
substances.uses: Acrylic fibres and the precursor for carbon fibre.
substances.notes: Heated and carbonised to make high-strength carbon fibre.

substances.name: Polyethylene glycol
substances.uses: Laxatives, drug formulation, cosmetics and laboratory precipitation of DNA.
substances.notes: Water-soluble and biocompatible; its chain length sets whether it is a liquid or a wax.

substances.name: Polyvinylpyrrolidone
substances.uses: Tablet binder, povidone-iodine antiseptic, and hair and food additive.
substances.notes: Dissolves in water and many solvents; used as a blood-plasma substitute in the Second World War.

substances.name: Polyacrylamide
substances.uses: Water-treatment flocculant, soil conditioner and gel-electrophoresis medium.
substances.notes: The polymer itself is low hazard, but its monomer acrylamide is neurotoxic.

substances.name: Polybutadiene
substances.uses: Synthetic rubber for tyres, golf-ball cores and toughening plastics.
substances.notes: A highly elastic diene rubber, often blended with other rubbers.

substances.name: Polysulfone
substances.uses: Membranes for water treatment, medical devices and heat-resistant parts.
substances.notes: A rigid, heat-stable engineering plastic built from sulfone and ether links.

substances.name: Phthalic acid
substances.uses: Precursor to phthalate plasticisers, dyes and polyester resins.
substances.notes: The ortho isomer of benzenedicarboxylic acid; terephthalic acid is the para isomer.

substances.name: Phthalates
substances.uses: Plasticisers that make PVC flexible; also used in cosmetics and coatings.
substances.notes: A family of dialkyl esters of phthalic acid; some members are endocrine disruptors under review.

substances.name: Perfluorooctanoic acid
substances.uses: Former fluoropolymer processing aid for nonstick coatings; legacy contaminant.
substances.notes: A persistent PFAS forever chemical that is largely phased out under the Stockholm Convention.

substances.name: Sodium oxalate
substances.uses: Standard for permanganate titrations; textile and metal-cleaning uses.
substances.notes: Toxic if swallowed and forms insoluble calcium oxalate with calcium ions.

substances.name: Ammonium oxalate
substances.uses: Analytical reagent for precipitating calcium; metal-polishing and cleaning.
substances.notes: A soluble oxalate salt that is harmful if swallowed.

substances.name: Sodium nitrite
substances.uses: Cured-meat preservative (E250) and antidote for cyanide poisoning.
substances.notes: Added to cured meat to stop botulism; can form nitrosamines when heated with amines.

substances.name: Calcium hypochlorite
substances.uses: Swimming-pool disinfectant and industrial bleaching agent.
substances.notes: A strong oxidiser that releases hypochlorous acid when dissolved in water.

substances.name: Ammonium dichromate
substances.uses: Historic volcanic-effect demonstrations and some oxidation catalysts.
substances.notes: A bright-orange oxidiser whose decomposition looks like a tiny volcano; its hexavalent chromium is carcinogenic.

substances.name: Sodium phosphate
substances.uses: Food additives (E339), buffers, cleaners and water treatment.
substances.notes: A family of sodium salts of phosphoric acid; trisodium phosphate is the alkaline cleaner.

substances.name: Potassium phosphate
substances.uses: Food additive (E340), fertiliser, buffer and chromatography mobile phase.
substances.notes: A family of potassium salts of phosphoric acid; KH2PO4 is a common laboratory buffer.

substances.name: Sodium lactate
substances.uses: Food preservative, moisture-holding cosmetic agent and intravenous fluid.
substances.notes: The sodium salt of lactic acid; a component of Ringer's lactate drips.

substances.name: Calcium gluconate
substances.uses: Calcium supplement and antidote for hydrofluoric-acid burns and high blood potassium.
substances.notes: Injectable and oral calcium source; its gel neutralises hydrogen fluoride burns.

substances.name: Potassium iodate
substances.uses: Iodised-salt additive that prevents goitre; flour oxidising agent.
substances.notes: A stable oxidiser used to give table salt its iodine.

substances.name: Potassium bromate
substances.uses: Historical flour improver; now banned in many countries.
substances.notes: A carcinogenic oxidiser that once gave bread a fine, even crumb.

substances.name: Phosphorus oxychloride
substances.uses: Vilsmeier formylation, dehydrations and phosphate-ester synthesis.
substances.notes: A fuming, moisture-sensitive liquid that hydrolyses to phosphoric acid and hydrogen chloride.

substances.name: Trichloroethylene
substances.uses: Industrial degreaser for metal parts and dry-cleaning solvent.
substances.notes: A volatile chlorinated solvent linked to cancer and Parkinson's disease and now tightly regulated.

substances.name: Perchloroethylene
substances.uses: Dry-cleaning solvent and metal degreaser.
substances.notes: A dense, non-flammable chlorocarbon that is a probable carcinogen under review.

substances.name: NADP-dependent enzyme cofactors
substances.uses: Provide reducing power (NADPH) for biosynthesis and antioxidant defence.
substances.notes: A class of cofactors: enzymes such as fatty-acid synthase and glutathione reductase recycle NADP+ and NADPH.

substances.name: Cyclic AMP
substances.uses: Second messenger for hormones such as adrenaline; controls metabolism and gene activity.
substances.notes: Made from ATP by adenylyl cyclase; a classic signalling molecule.

substances.name: Cyclic GMP
substances.uses: Second messenger for nitric-oxide signalling; relaxes blood vessels.
substances.notes: Drugs such as sildenafil work by slowing the breakdown of cGMP.

substances.name: S-Adenosylmethionine
substances.uses: Principal methyl-group donor in biology; also sold as a supplement.
substances.notes: Made from methionine and ATP; methylates DNA, proteins and small molecules.

substances.name: Carnosine
substances.uses: Muscle antioxidant and pH buffer; sold for exercise performance.
substances.notes: A dipeptide of beta-alanine and histidine concentrated in muscle and brain.

substances.name: Oxytocin
substances.uses: Induces labour and controls postpartum bleeding; also involved in social bonding.
substances.notes: A nine-amino-acid cyclic peptide made in the hypothalamus.

substances.name: Vasopressin
substances.uses: Controls water retention and blood pressure; used for diabetes insipidus and shock.
substances.notes: Also called antidiuretic hormone; a nonapeptide released by the pituitary gland.

substances.name: Pyrrole
substances.uses: Precursor to conducting polypyrrole, porphyrins, and drugs.
substances.notes: Aromatic five-membered ring with one NH; the nitrogen lone pair is part of the ring, so it is not basic.

substances.name: Furan
substances.uses: Chemical building block; parent of furanose sugars and furfural; used in resins.
substances.notes: Aromatic five-membered oxygen ring; made industrially from furfural.

substances.name: Thiophene
substances.uses: Building block for dyes, drugs, and conducting polymers; occurs in petroleum and coal tar.
substances.notes: Aromatic sulfur analogue of furan; the sulfur lone pair participates in the aromatic system.

substances.name: Pyridine
substances.uses: Solvent and base; precursor to drugs, pesticides, niacin, and dyes.
substances.notes: Aromatic six-membered ring with a basic nitrogen; the lone pair is not part of the ring pi system.

substances.name: Imidazole
substances.uses: Pharmaceutical building block; side chain of histidine and histamine; buffer component.
substances.notes: Five-membered ring with two nitrogens, one basic and one acidic.

substances.name: Pyrazole
substances.uses: Core of anti-inflammatory drugs such as celecoxib and many agrochemicals.
substances.notes: Aromatic five-membered ring with two adjacent nitrogen atoms.

substances.name: Oxazole
substances.uses: Scaffold in medicinal chemistry and fluorescent dyes.
substances.notes: Aromatic five-membered ring with one oxygen and one nitrogen separated by a carbon.

substances.name: Isoxazole
substances.uses: Drug and agrochemical scaffold; used as a diene precursor in synthesis.
substances.notes: Aromatic five-membered ring with adjacent oxygen and nitrogen atoms.

substances.name: Thiazole
substances.uses: Vitamin B1 (thiamine) and many drug scaffolds; flavor and dye chemistry.
substances.notes: Aromatic ring with sulfur and nitrogen; parent of thiamine.

substances.name: Isothiazole
substances.uses: Active core of some biocides and pharmaceuticals.
substances.notes: Aromatic five-membered ring with adjacent sulfur and nitrogen.

substances.name: 1,2,3-Triazole
substances.uses: Product of click chemistry; found in drugs and specialty materials.
substances.notes: Five-membered ring with three nitrogens; formed by the Huisgen azide-alkyne cycloaddition.

substances.name: 1,2,4-Triazole
substances.uses: Fungicide and pharmaceutical scaffold.
substances.notes: Aromatic five-membered ring with three nitrogens; a common bioisostere of amides.

substances.name: Tetrazole
substances.uses: Explosive and propellant chemistry; carboxylate bioisostere in drugs.
substances.notes: Five-membered ring with four nitrogens; highly acidic NH.

substances.name: Pyrimidine
substances.uses: Parent of the nucleobases cytosine, thymine, and uracil; drug scaffold.
substances.notes: Aromatic six-membered ring with two nitrogens at positions 1 and 3.

substances.name: Pyrazine
substances.uses: Flavor and fragrance (roasted, cocoa notes); drug scaffold.
substances.notes: Aromatic six-membered ring with nitrogens opposite each other.

substances.name: Pyridazine
substances.uses: Drug and agrochemical building block.
substances.notes: Aromatic six-membered ring with adjacent nitrogen atoms.

substances.name: 1,3,5-Triazine
substances.uses: Core of herbicides such as atrazine and the monomer for melamine resins.
substances.notes: Aromatic six-membered ring with three alternating nitrogens.

substances.name: Indole
substances.uses: Parent of tryptophan, serotonin, and many alkaloids and dyes.
substances.notes: Benzene ring fused to pyrrole; the NH is weakly acidic.

substances.name: Isoindole
substances.uses: Building block for dyes, pigments, and pharmaceuticals.
substances.notes: Benzene fused to pyrrole at the 2,3 positions.

substances.name: Quinoline
substances.uses: Antimalarials such as quinine and chloroquine; dyes and solvents.
substances.notes: Benzene fused to pyridine; the nitrogen is basic.

substances.name: Isoquinoline
substances.uses: Alkaloid parent (morphine, papaverine); pharmaceutical scaffold.
substances.notes: Benzene fused to pyridine at adjacent positions.

substances.name: Benzofuran
substances.uses: Drug scaffold (amiodarone); occurs in coal tar.
substances.notes: Benzene fused to furan.

substances.name: Benzothiophene
substances.uses: Pharmaceutical scaffold; desulfurization target in fuels.
substances.notes: Benzene fused to thiophene; found in petroleum.

substances.name: Benzimidazole
substances.uses: Anthelmintics (albendazole) and proton-pump inhibitors (omeprazole).
substances.notes: Benzene fused to imidazole; also a vitamin B12 ligand.

substances.name: Indazole
substances.uses: Kinase-inhibitor drug scaffold.
substances.notes: Benzene fused to pyrazole.

substances.name: Purine
substances.uses: Parent of adenine and guanine; caffeine and uric acid are purines.
substances.notes: Bicyclic ring of pyrimidine fused to imidazole.

substances.name: Pteridine
substances.uses: Parent of folic acid and the flavin coenzymes; pigment chemistry.
substances.notes: Bicyclic system of pyrazine fused to pyrimidine.

substances.name: Carbazole
substances.uses: Dye and photoconductor precursor; OLED materials.
substances.notes: Two benzene rings fused to pyrrole.

substances.name: Acridine
substances.uses: Dyes and antiseptics; DNA-intercalating drugs.
substances.notes: Three fused six-membered rings with a central pyridine; fluorescent.

substances.name: Phenothiazine
substances.uses: Parent of antipsychotic drugs such as chlorpromazine; insecticide and dye.
substances.notes: Sulfur and nitrogen linked by two benzene rings.

substances.name: Phenoxazine
substances.uses: Core of oxazine dyes and organic electronics.
substances.notes: Oxygen and nitrogen joined by two benzene rings.

substances.name: Coumarin
substances.uses: Fragrance (tonka bean); parent of the anticoagulant warfarin.

substances.notes: A dithiol chelator that binds heavy metals.

substances.name: Dimercaprol
substances.uses: Antidote for arsenic, mercury, and gold poisoning.
substances.notes: Developed as an antidote to the arsenic war gas lewisite.

substances.name: Deferoxamine
substances.uses: Iron and aluminium overload.
